title: Asset Allocation and the 60/40 Rule
content: Asset allocation is the strategy of dividing investments among different asset categories—such as equities, fixed-income bonds, and cash equivalents. The classic 60/40 portfolio allocates 60% to equities for capital appreciation and 40% to bonds for income and downside volatility protection.

title: Portfolio Rebalancing
content: Rebalancing involves periodically buying or selling portions of your portfolio to maintain your target asset allocation. If equities surge, they may grow from 60% to 75% of your portfolio, exposing you to higher risk. Rebalancing brings the mix back to target, enforcing buying low and selling high.

title: Expense Ratios and Fee Drag
content: An expense ratio is the annual percentage fee charged by funds to manage your money. An expense ratio of 1% on a $100,000 portfolio costs $1,000/year, compounding over decades into tens of thousands of dollars lost compared to low-cost index funds charging 0.03% to 0.08%.
